title: Predictive throttle and fairness guardrails for slot starvation during burst-coupled loads
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: After a capacity event on 2025-10-29 we observed sustained tail-latency spikes and request starvation for lower-priority lanes. Investigation showed a coupling between the adaptive slot allocator and transient load bursts that allowed high-priority, high-token-rate streams to consume most slot budget for long windows. This ticket captures the mitigations we implemented and the follow-up engineering work to prevent recurrence, including a predictive throttling mechanism, per-lane fairness guardrails, and new observability to detect load coupling early.
incident_summary: During a multi-region capacity constriction, the continuous batcher entered a state where the slot allocator kept renewing allocations to a small set of high-throughput streams. This produced long-lived batches with imbalanced composition, inflating tail latencies and causing lower-priority customer requests to queue for >3s. The incident lasted ~47 minutes before automated fallback and manual interventions restored equitable batching behavior.
timeline:
2025-10-29 09:12 UTC: first latency alerts on prod-rt-us-east.
2025-10-29 09:18 UTC: spike in high-priority token throughput correlated with a third-party data flood.
2025-10-29 09:25 UTC: continuous batcher metrics show slot reuse ratio > 92% for top 3 shards.
2025-10-29 09:40 UTC: automated fallback to single-tenant small batches triggered for affected instances.
2025-10-29 09:58 UTC: rate-limit adjustments and temporary per-customer token caps applied.
2025-10-29 09:59-10:00 UTC: tail latencies return to normal baseline.
2025-10-29 10:00-10:59 UTC: controlled mitigations and monitoring until full recovery confirmed.
impact: Affected several mid-sized customers in us-east region; some product features experienced delayed responses and timeouts. No data loss. Estimated lost revenue risk minimal but degraded SLAs for 47 minutes.
root_cause: The slot allocation algorithm favored streams with sustained high token rates but lacked a predictive mechanism to detect burst-coupling across priority lanes. Under constrained GPU capacity the allocator kept assigning slots to hot streams because historical utilization looked healthy, leading to starvation of other lanes. Additionally, the absence of an early warning metric for cross-lane coupling delayed automated fallback triggers.
immediate_mitigation: Applied conservative per-customer token caps to limit sustained consumption while preserving best-effort throughput for others
Enabled emergency single-tenant batching mode for the 3 most impacted instances to break the long-lived batch cycles
Adjusted autoscaler thresholds to allow faster reactive capacity for short bursts (temporary knob change)
Rolled out a hotfix that propagates backpressure signals from batch-formation to upstream request routers
long_term_actions: Implement predictive throttle that uses short-window token-velocity + burst coupling score to temporarily limit slot renewals for hot streams
Add fairness guardrails: enforce minimum slot reservation quotas per priority lane under constrained capacity
Introduce a cross-lane coupling metric and dashboard with automated alerts when coupling > threshold
Extend continuous-batcher test harness to simulate mixed-priority burst patterns and validate fairness under autoscaler constraints
Build a canary experiment to validate predictive throttle on 10% of traffic before global rollout
acceptance_criteria: New predictive throttle deployed behind a feature flag with documented config knobs
Observed reduction in 99.9th percentile latency for lower-priority lanes by at least 40% in controlled fault-injection tests
Cross-lane coupling metric has an alert and has been tested to fire during synthetic burst scenarios
Post-deploy runbook updated and on-call trained for the new mitigation surface
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged rollout. If new throttle causes unacceptable throughput degradation for P0 customers, toggle feature flag off and revert autoscaler knob to previous values. Post-rollback, run postmortem tie-out tests and limit rollout scope.
